units.translation: The tragedians sometimes said ἁπλάκημα [a fault] and ἀπλακεῖν [to have erred] where the first syllable needed to be short. Once Aeschylus Eum. 934 τὰ γὰρ ἐκ προτέρων ἀπλακήματα [for the faults from earlier times]. Thus Pauwius for ἀμπλακήματα [faults].
I pay the penalty for such faults.
This fault will seem to be mine.
For what faults do you pay penalties?
And there Zeus judges the faults.
And the fault belongs to the one who transgresses the ordinance.
For the faults from earlier times
For whose fault do you perish by penalties?
And he whirls the horses, snorting in their frontlets.
Her cheek is conspicuous, stained with blood from lacerations.
A satyr play of Aeschylus was entitled Amymone (fr. 11-13).
(infinitive of a verb with middle forms), whose middle form is ἀμυναθέσθαι [to ward off for oneself],
Aeschylus uses it Eum. 438 τόνδ᾽ ἀμυναθοῦ ψόγον [ward off this reproach], where M has the wrong accent ἀμυνάθου [ward off].
of a verb with middle forms
so as neither to flee nor to ward off death.
The mind is lacerated by fear.

(where the Attic form ἀμφήκει [sharp] has been substituted for the Doric form in the copies. Hesychius noted the Doric form ἀμφάκης: ἀξίνη [two-edged: axe], which gloss is perhaps to be referred to Soph. El. 485, where in the codex ἀμφήκης [sharp] is read.)
a lock of fire, sharp on both sides.
a preposition that is construed with the genitive, dative, and accusative.
[Suppl. 806 ἀμφ᾿ αὐτὰς [around them] is a faulty reading, about which I have spoken under the word αλλύτας.]
where ἀμφ' ἐμοί [around me] is rather to be written: see Lex. Soph. p. 134.
as περὶ τάρβει [with fear] (or φόβῳ [with fear]) Pers. 696. Ch. 35. and ἀμφὶ φόβῳ [with fear] Eur. Or. 825.
[Ag. 715 αἰῶν᾽ ἀμφὶ [life around] is corrupt from αἰῶνα φίλον [dear life]: see under the word αἰών.]
|| ἀμφί [around] in tmesis. See ἀμφικυκλόω [to encircle].
as she leads the contest around herself.
Thus it has been commanded to speak about this.
Why have you lamented these things about Loxias?
She seems likely to prophesy about her own evils.
And about herself you utter a lawless song.
He persuaded with such a speech about us.
that they have no authority about you.
about a woman of many husbands he will set many wrestling-bouts.
weeping for the torch-carrying rites around you.
with strong force he struck with a hammer around the hands.
he threw the arm-pin fasteners around the sides.
she tears her robes around her body,
But are you weaving some trick around me, stranger?
hearing of the dishonor of her child around her body, of her garments.
who once hurled a missile around me.
wolves carry a fawn under their arms.
and fear is around the eyes.
